title: RAW frozen38 Galen extension: complete f80v naming dispute with actual, advocated and as-if scopes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT A SEMANTIC TEST. Second of three predeclared whole-paragraph attempts: all33 ZL3b groups on f80v.19–22 receive a complete exploratory reading of owned GalenII.44.5 plus two explicit §4 recaps. All38 parent499 values remain verbatim fixed;8 recur at10 positions and21 new values cover23 positions. Three fitted productions, an unmarked lettuce/reportability aside, new TO/OF typed embeddings and explicit modal/audience scopes are charged. A global actual-name table still survives; no independent semantic confirmation or IT2a reading is claimed.

work.author: Galen
work.date: Second-century CE work. A complete medieval Latin translation is documented in1277; the work date is not inferred from a Renaissance print.
work.title: De alimentorum facultatibus / Περὶ τῶν ἐν ταῖς τροφαῖς δυνάμεων
work.digital_text_attribution: Open Greek and Latin, First1KGreek, based on Helmreich1923. Digital conversion/editing credits appear in the whole XML header. Digital text license: CC BY-SA4.0; ancient Greek and1923 edition are public domain.
work.medieval_reception_scope: The scholarly catalog gives a complete Moerbeke translation finished1277-10-22 and pre1450 witnesses. No Latin passage or native medieval folio collation is claimed.

section.greek: τοῦτο τὸ λάχανον οἱ τὴν ἐπίτριπτον ψευδοπαιδείαν ἀϲκοῦντεϲ ὀνομάζειν ἀξιοῦϲι ῥάφανον, ὥϲπερ τοῖϲ πρὸ ἑξακοϲίων ἐτῶν Ἀθηναίοιϲ διαλεγομένων ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ τοῖϲ νῦν Ἕλληϲιν, οἷϲ ἅπαϲιν ἔθοϲ ἐϲτὶν ἐπ’ ἄλλου φυτοῦ τὸ τῆϲ ῥαφάνου ὄνομα φέρειν.
section.english_working_translation: Those who practise tiresome sham learning think fit to call this vegetable rhaphanos, as though we were speaking to Athenians of six hundred years ago rather than to present-day Greeks, all of whom customarily apply the name rhaphanos to another plant.
section.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

complete_source.scope: All of II.44.5, not a single naming phrase. The full five-section parent remains unchanged.

source_obligations: The criticized group practising sham learning insists on naming the same vegetable rhaphanos.
The author compares this to addressing Athenians of600 years before his own present.
The intended present audience is contemporary Greeks, not that old audience.
All those contemporary Greeks customarily use that same name rhaphanos for a different unnamed plant.
The name is identical across the disputed uses, while food/plant referents and audience/time contexts differ.

development_claim_scope_correction.earlier_preselection_wording: The same named CABBAGE food can retain its old nourishment/juice properties while a speech community assigns the same term to another plant. A global name→one-plant lookup loses the audience/time scope; the other plant must remain unnamed.
development_claim_scope_correction.correction: The early claim that a global name-to-one-plant lookup loses the relevant content was too strong if it means an actual-use function. P only advocates the name for C, while customary use for R is asserted. A global actual-name function t→R is compatible with both. The new complete content consists of the modal contrast, the same name and distinct plant arguments, and the rhetorical audience comparison; it does not force two actual customary referents.

selected_target.scope: Entire four-line paragraph. No crop, word deletion, uncertainty cleanup or movement of physical word boundaries. Clause groupings below are new grammar assumptions, not manuscript sentence boundaries.

frozen_parent_lexicon.denotation: The two specified foods have similar drying action. This compound does not supply their identities, the sight consequence or the exception.
The specified drying action is the author’s stated cause of the specified sight dulling; not an empirical or modern mechanism claim.
Dulling of the specified faculty, here sight; no additional harm or numerical degree.
Same directed relation at4 and31: dulling targets sight; nourishment is supplied to the body. No change to a causal connector at31.
Human visual faculty, distinct from a physical eye and from nourishment.
The guard removes the otherwise stated consequence from the claim’s scope; it does not assert the opposite effect when the guard holds.
The entire relevant eye; not the whole human body or just an unspecified wet surface.
The following moisture is beyond the relevant natural condition. No quantitative threshold is given.
Copular application; identical denotation at9,34,38. It does not select a new subject or change the property.

frozen_parent_lexicon.type: attributed entity → ordered qualitative moisture attribute
frozen_parent_lexicon.denotation: One moisture attribute at10/12: abnormal moisture of the eye and comparative moisture of nourishment. The two kinds are not numerically equated or directly compared with each other.
Resumes the two topic foods CABBAGE and LENTIL, whose explicit names appear later. This backward topic binding is an assumption, not two newly found plant names.

Generic food consequence/profile. At13 the comparison context selects the nourishment profile; at49/51 the explicit urinary predicates select urinary-effect propositions. It does not itself mean either NOURISHMENT or URINE.
Same food type at14/28/37/40/55; no new physical serving per occurrence and no assertion that distinct source comparisons involve one consumed object.

frozen_parent_lexicon.type: ordered attribute value × same-kind value → strict comparison
frozen_parent_lexicon.denotation: First bound comparison operand is greater than the second. Here the compared attribute is MOIST; no quantity, total effect strength or duration is silently substituted.
Introduces the second comparator supplied by the declared C02 syntax.
The nourishment profile supplied by a food, with amount, moisture and texture/humoral descriptors. Not identical to its intrinsic juice.
The lentil/lentil-soup food type in the owned working source. This is a guessed name; it does not identify a depicted botanical specimen.
Same OF relation at19 and41. In the postpositional owner convention, NOURISHMENT LENTIL OF means N(L), and CABBAGE OF at40/41 supplies the owner of the active juice profile J(C).
Exact copular synonym of qoky. At20 it predicates LITTLE of N(C), at22 VEGETABLE of C, and at53 VEGETABLE of C; syntax supplies subjects.
Little nourishment. No numerical amount or proportional effect on the eye is supplied.

frozen_parent_lexicon.type: food → kind predicate or its nominal restriction
frozen_parent_lexicon.denotation: Vegetable as a food kind, repeated23/46/54 for the same cabbage type. Nominal use identifies the already active vegetable C; it is not a filler or a new plant.
The vegetable/not-solid-food classification supplies the stated reason for the nourishment contrast. This does not introduce a second medical effect.
Boolean negation, here of SOLID_FOOD(C).
The source’s solid-food category, not all food. A vegetable is still a food in the declared type hierarchy.
One conjunction at27/42: vegetable plus not-solid-food classification; bad plus foul-smelling juice properties. No sequencing or comparison meaning.
Exact freely guessed synonym of qokain, retaining the same food type.
Exact freely guessed synonym of saiiin.
The human body receiving nourishment, not the cabbage’s solid body from sourceII.44.1 and not the eye alone.
Considerable nourishment, without a number. The little/much contrast concerns the same nourishment-amount dimension, not moisture.
One compound property conjunction: thick and melancholic. Both descriptors are retained; no modern chemical or psychiatric interpretation is asserted.
Exact freely guessed synonym of sshey. It negates good-juicedness at36 and the stated disjunction of reportability propositions at47.

The food has good intrinsic juice. This adjective presupposes a juice profile J(food); negation denies its GOOD quality, not the existence of juice. That internal constituent projection is an explicit cost.
Bad quality of the bound entity/profile; main C04 applies it to J(C). The lexical predicate alone does not determine owner or exclude application to a whole food.
Foul-smelling quality; main C04 applies it to the same J(C) as BAD. No medical effect follows.
The lettuce comparator named in the source; positive good-juiced contrast comes from the explicit C04 construction, not from the name itself.

The author can state a manifest result of the specified kind. Under NOT this is lack of warranted reportability, not proof of no physical effect and not an inability of every observer to know anything.
A manifest beneficial urinary consequence from the bound food. The source author’s ability to state it is separately scoped; the word does not assert it actually occurs.
A manifest harmful urinary consequence from the same bound food. This is a second compound descriptor, not an actual adverse event.

new_lexicon.denotation: The source-criticized practitioners of tiresome sham learning. This composite group description does not itself say what name they advocate, name a plant or assert their actual language use.

new_lexicon.type: group × plant × Name → advocated naming proposition
new_lexicon.denotation: The group thinks fit or insists that the given plant be called the supplied name. Normative/advocatory force; it does not entail actual or customary use. External group, plant and name arguments are mandatory.
The already introduced cabbage food-kind C, with its VEGETABLE restriction. No new serving or different vegetable.
The Greek name rhaphanos as an object of the source naming dispute. This is one unconfirmed whole-form guess, with no phonetic derivation.

The author presents the supplied speaking situation as a rhetorical as-if comparison. It does not assert that speakers really address the historical group or that the historical group actually uses the advocated name.
The source-authorial we speaks in the specified audience frame. The speech output and its recipient relation are arguments supplied by the construction, not encoded names.
Ordinary propositional negation, here inside the rhetorical audience frame. This is an additional exact spelling of the same NOT value already guessed for sol/sshey.
The Greeks contemporary with the Galen source-author at reference time tau0. Neither present-day Greeks nor a date of Voynich composition.
The same lettuce food-kind as old char=LETTUCE. An explicitly counted new synonymous form, not a new plant or new physical serving.
Athenians at the time supplied by the temporal modifier. It does not supply an ancient naming custom.
Six hundred years before the Galen source-present tau0, qualifying ATHENIANS. A composite interval/deictic value, without an absolute date or inferred manuscript chronology.
Every member of the explicitly supplied group, here G. This is the source author’s generic assertion, not a new census or observation.
Resume the one explicitly introduced name t=RHAPHANOS. Identical denotation and antecedent at positions18 and24; no new name is created at the second use.
The identical community G at tau0 denoted by ysheeyqorar. This second spelling is separately counted, not assumed to derive morphologically.
The supplied group customarily uses the specified name for the specified plant. This modifier does not silently change an advocated usage into an actual one.

new_lexicon.type: group/person × Name × plant → structured name-use content
new_lexicon.denotation: Build the same name-use content U(user,name,plant) at both occurrences. Its actuality, customary status or placement under INSIST is supplied by written outer operators, not by a per-occurrence word change. The construction may expose the content’s directed naming output and plant-owned naming profile, under separately declared assumptions.

new_lexicon.type: Plant reference R relative to C
new_lexicon.denotation: A plant R distinct from the source’s current cabbage C. The source does not identify it further. R is not automatically RADISH, a vegetable food or edible.
The supplied group thinks fit or insists on the supplied naming content. This does not assert actual or customary performance.
The same source-criticized group P introduced by PEDANTS_SHAM_LEARNING. No second group or present-day criticism is introduced.
The already active food-kind C, explicitly restated by CABBAGE. It does not denote the other unnamed plant R.
Ordinary propositional negation. Same NOT operator as oltydy and old sol/sshey; here it denies SOLID_FOOD(C), not C’s existence or vegetable status.

binding_assumptions.content: RHAPHANOS4 introduces a Name object t. SAME_NAME18/24 resumes exactly t. OTHER_PLANT22 introduces R:Plant with R≠C; no stronger identification or Food coercion of R is allowed.

binding_assumptions.content: PEDANTS_SHAM_LEARNING1 introduces P, resumed by PEDANTS26. CURRENT_GREEKS8/19 is G at the same source-present tau0. Both group-reference equalities are guessed binding rules, not text-confirmed identity.

binding_assumptions.name: Finite whole productions
binding_assumptions.content: C01 owns positions1–16 including an embedded aside10–12; C02 owns17–22; C03 owns23–33. The three exact fitted productions are the whole reading, not a demonstrated productive grammar. Source §5 is restated with an extra repeat of P’s proposal and two §4 recaps.

binding_assumptions.name: Unmarked parenthetical aside
binding_assumptions.content: Positions10–12 form the complete aside CAN_STATE_MANIFEST(S,GOOD_JUICED(T)) inside C01’s audience construction. No written punctuation or independent boundary confirms this interruption. Those three tokens are consumed once, not ignored or assigned to two clauses.

binding_assumptions.name: Local positive reportability assumption
binding_assumptions.content: Parent499 asserts GOOD_JUICED(T) as a source comparison. This draft additionally asserts that S can state that quality as a manifest result. The old CAN_STATE_MANIFEST denotation stays reportability of a specified kind; intrinsic-juice quality is here admitted as such a result. Assertion of GOOD_JUICED alone does not logically entail this capability, and no general rule that all source assertions are manifest is adopted. If this local assumption is rejected, the aside has a concrete unbound old-value obligation.

binding_assumptions.name: Speech output as recipient-bearing output
binding_assumptions.content: SPEAK6 supplies an output sigma. Old TO retains the directed output-to-recipient relation; speech is explicitly admitted as an output, G and the historical Athenians as recipients. This new domain embedding is an assumption beyond parent499’s sight/body applications.

binding_assumptions.name: Two audience orders with fixed TO
binding_assumptions.content: In the C01 frame, NOT7 CURRENT_GREEKS8 TO9 gives NOT(TO(sigma_cf,G)); TO14 ATHENIANS15 supplies TO(sigma_cf,A_old). Prefix and postposed occurrence order both map to the same directed relation, never to a cause or conjunction. This fitted ordering difference is charged explicitly.

binding_assumptions.name: Fixed conjunction and rhetorical scope
binding_assumptions.content: Old AND13 conjoins the two audience propositions, not their noun phrases and not the lettuce aside. AS_IF5 places NOT(TO(sigma_cf,G)) AND TO(sigma_cf,A_old) inside a rhetorical comparison attached to P’s proposal. No actual conversation with ancient Athenians or actual ancient naming use is asserted.

binding_assumptions.name: Rhetorical alternative and source-present
binding_assumptions.content: The contrastive AS_IF construction sets G as the author’s real intended audience and A_old as the imagined audience. This positive alternative is supplied by the fitted contrast construction, not deduced from bare NOT. SIX_HUNDRED_YEARS_AGO16 qualifies A_old relative to Galen’s tau0, not a manuscript date.

binding_assumptions.name: Quantifier and customary-use scope
binding_assumptions.content: C02 ALL17 binds members g of G19; SAME_NAME18 supplies t, OTHER_PLANT22 supplies R. CUSTOMARILY20 scopes U(g,t,R) from USE_NAME21. Universal generic customary use is the author’s assertion; no universal statement about every actual utterance or time is inferred.

binding_assumptions.name: Advocated calling and name-use bridge
binding_assumptions.content: INSIST_CALL(P,C,t) in C01 and INSIST(P,U(P,t,C)) in C03 are locally declared equivalent descriptions of the same advocated naming. This bridge costs an extra construction. Neither entails that P has actually performed a naming act; C03 is a deliberate redundant restatement.

binding_assumptions.name: Fronted food topic and supplied subject
binding_assumptions.content: C03’s VEGETABLE23 is the old nominal restriction identifying C; SAME_NAME24 gives t, INSIST25 takes group P26 and U27 as content. THIS_FOOD30 and CABBAGE32 are the same C, not R or lettuce. This reference span is explicit, not automatic nearest-noun resolution.

binding_assumptions.name: Name-use output and food-owned profile
binding_assumptions.content: Inside C03’s advocated U(P,t,C), the construction exposes naming output out(U) and naming profile profile(U). TO28 targets out(U) to C; OF29 owns profile(U) by C. These are two explicitly projected relations, both using THIS_FOOD30/CABBAGE32 as an argument. Admitting a name-use profile as a dependent profile of its target food and a food as recipient of naming output is a new typed embedding, not inherited evidence. R receives no OF or FOOD predicate. If this embedding fails review, retain the whole extension’s concrete TO/OF binding gap; do not weaken the parent denotations.

binding_assumptions.name: Prefix ownership and shared argument
binding_assumptions.content: OF29 THIS_FOOD30 is a newly declared prefix ownership construction, while parent499 used postpositional ownership. TO28 and OF29 share C explicitly rather than deleting one as filler. The parent postpositional examples remain fixed; no parser is retrospectively repaired.

binding_assumptions.name: Negative food recap
binding_assumptions.content: NOT31 CABBAGE32 SOLID_FOOD33 is a subject-interposed negated predicate NOT(SOLID_FOOD(C)), with an implicit copula. It restates parent499’s classification and remains outside the INSIST attitude; the cabbage food remains a vegetable. No naming belief changes C’s nutrition or intrinsic juice.

binding_assumptions.name: Counted synonyms and composite values
binding_assumptions.content: cheey is a new synonym of char=LETTUCE; ysheeyqorar/y both denote CURRENT_GREEKS; oltydy/or both add forms for old NOT. PEDANTS26 resumes the descriptive P at1. Ten new entries are charged as semantically composite: psheoldy,dkshey,qokopy,ysheeyqorar,tar,okal,y,qokal,olor,dal. None provides a full multi-argument source assertion without external arguments.

binding_assumptions.name: Source modality and full-unit boundary
binding_assumptions.content: All II.44.5 is represented, including the criticized group, naming advocacy, source-relative old-Athenian audience, current Greeks, universal customary use and different unnamed plant. C01 aside and C03 food recap are extra content linked to §4. No new physical medical result, all-five-section reading, modern historical truth or global decipherment is claimed.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Retain a single actual-name function t→R for current customary use; retain P’s advocacy for C as an attitude whose content need not be true or actually used.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: No actual two-referent name ambiguity is entailed. This rival is compatible with the main source reading, so success cannot select a context-dependent actual dictionary.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Keep P advocacy, G customary usage and the old-Athenian rhetorical comparison, but do not project a separate actual speaking event or independently asserted ancient name-use table from AS_IF.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: Current intended audience may remain a pragmatic source context rather than an asserted actual speaking event. Main also asserts no actual time travel or ancient naming table. A future check must not score the absent ancient fact as a failure.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Keep the old positive GOOD_JUICED(T) source assertion and all old CAN_STATE_MANIFEST meanings, but withhold the new B06 local reportability assumption.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: No entitlement to the positive CAN_STATE_MANIFEST(S,GOOD_JUICED(T)) aside; old shey12 remains an additional target obligation. This is not evidence that the lettuce quality or whole family is false.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Keep the exact old output-recipient and dependent-profile/food-owner relations but allow only their previously licensed physical/profile applications, declining B07/B14’s speech/naming embeddings.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: The new TO/OF occurrences remain unbound; this is a failure of the extension construction, not an automatic contradiction in the old lexicon. Do not rescue it by renaming TO or OF.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Convert P’s advocated U(P,t,C) into an asserted actual naming custom.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: Would add an actual usage assertion absent from the source. An executable control may expose that difference, but rejecting this alteration cannot by itself establish a manuscript reading.

serious_fixed_alternatives.definition: Identify R with C despite explicit OTHER_PLANT and the source’s other-plant relation.
serious_fixed_alternatives.different_consequence: Would erase the source’s written referent distinction. Kept as a simple ownership check, not promoted as the serious rival.
